correctness.rationale: Conditioning on shift gives exact independent escape product over all integer lattice sites. Exterior sites contribute at most (L+1)/(1-eta) to minus log probability by Tonelli counting of integer sites in a length-L window, with eta<1 from positive masses on both signs. For inside sites, log sum of two one-sided escape terms differs from min of their tail costs by ≤log2, and uniform logarithmic tail equivalents control the interior bulk plus O(1) boundary sites. Shifted-grid Riemann sum then yields integral min(c_- x^alpha,c_+(1-x)^alpha) and sharp crossover theta=c_+^{1/alpha}/(c_-^{1/alpha}+c_+^{1/alpha}); uniform shift and stationarization follow by exponential sandwich. Gaussian Mills asymptotic gives I=1/(24 sigma²). Four parameter coefficient checks corroborate; no finite computation proves L→∞.

value.rationale: A sharp large-void exponent with exact asymmetric left/right tail coefficient for a canonical perturbed lattice is a natural stochastic geometry invariant, improving known exponent-order hole bounds. The Gaussian 1/(24σ²) specialization is concrete and the left-right escape transition gives interpretable structure.

final_claim: For iid atomless 1D lattice displacements with logarithmic one-sided tails -log P(Y>t)~c_+ t^alpha and -log P(Y<-t)~c_- t^alpha, alpha>0 and c±>0, stationary and any fixed shift u have -log P(no points in [0,L])/L^{alpha+1} tending to I=c_-c_+/((alpha+1)(c_-^{1/alpha}+c_+^{1/alpha})^alpha); Gaussian I=1/(24 sigma²).
